## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix `finished_at` before merge because the new field reports a start time as a finish time for a process whose only event is `started`.

## Changes

The pull request adds `finished_at` to the current-state model and documents it in the schema catalog. The model still returns one row per process from its latest event.

## Critical

- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Stop reporting start times as finish times — For process 20, whose only event is `started`, `finished_at` returns that event’s `occurred_at` even though no finish was recorded. The source permits `created`, `started`, and `cleared` events and defines no distinct finish event. — Consumers using `finished_at` to identify completed processes will count this process as finished as soon as it starts. — Fix: Define which source event represents completion, or rename the field and its description to match the event it exposes.

## Important

- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the documented meaning of NULL — Process 30 has a `started` event followed by `cleared`, so `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` returns NULL for its latest row, contradicting “NULL means the process has never been started.” — Consumers who use NULL to identify processes that never started will also include previously started processes whose latest event is `cleared`.

## Suggestions

- models/schema.yml:12 — comments — Document that the source offset is preserved — If a latest `started` event supplies `2026-01-01T01:00:00+01:00`, `then occurred_at` returns that text verbatim, contradicting “Stored in UTC using the source event timestamp.” The source column accepts text without an offset constraint. — Consumers expecting UTC strings receive mixed offsets when source writers supply them.
- models/processes.sql:10 — tests — Test the timestamp for a created-only process — Process 10 has only a `created` event and takes the new expression’s NULL branch. The source fixture seeds that input, but no test asserts the model result. — A regression that populates `finished_at` for a created-only process would go undetected.
